episode.title: A Tornado Wider Than a City Over Kansas

synopsis: An impossibly vast tornado, spanning several kilometers, grinds slowly across the flat farmlands of Kansas, dwarfing entire towns and grain elevators beneath its cyclonic base.

shots.prompt:

caption:
A gigantic tornado, wider than any city, grinds slowly across the flat farmland grid of Kansas, USA.

The impossible tornado is over 5 kilometers wide, its immense base dwarfing entire rural towns and iconic grain elevators beneath its cyclonic fury.

The widest tornado on record, the 2013 El Reno tornado, was 4.2 kilometers wide but short-lived. Most powerful tornadoes are typically 1-2 kilometers wide.

The formation of such an immense supercell would require atmospheric shear and instability on a planetary scale. The energy required to sustain a rotating column of air this wide, resisting dissipation, is astronomical, demanding sustained updrafts and pressure differentials far beyond Earth's capabilities.

This is a simulation, not real footage.

How much destruction would a tornado this size cause to the landscape?
